resources.string: Cut right through the part, however thick it is or becomes.
Only a Cut can go through all: an Add or the first shape of a part needs a distance.
There is no material on that side to cut through. Flip the cut into the part.
That edge is where two features meet, not an outside edge of the part, so it cannot be rounded or bevelled.
Extrude up to a face of the part. Tap another face of the part to end there instead.
To Face ends an Add or a Cut on a face of the part parallel to the sketch, and there is none here.
That face cannot end this extrusion: choose a flat face of the same part made before it.
That face is not parallel to the sketch, so the extrusion cannot end on it.
There is no face of the part to reach on that side.
That is not an edge of the hole\'s face.
The two edges run the same way, so they cannot place the hole.
The sketch plane moved; the drawing moved with it.
That plane cannot be used: the angle must be within 90° and the offset within the sketch\'s reach, and only a sketch on a face of the part can stand off it.
Turn this shape into a CAD part of the same size and place, so holes, fillets and features can be added. Undo turns it back.
The shape is now a CAD part. Undo turns it back.
Only a box, a cylinder, a sphere or a cone that has not been sculpted can become a CAD part.
The extrusion shares no material with the part, so Intersect would leave nothing.
The extrusion holds the whole part, so Intersect would change nothing.
